alex: FYI CI alerted on the quantized bring-up run for redwood-open-3b-q8 — NDCG is slightly up but MRR tanked on a few datasets. link: https://ci.internal/runs/1869001220 :thinking_face:

mira: ugh. can you paste the eval summary and the exact command the runner used? also which artifact (q8) did CI pick up?

alex: pasted the job summary here and the runner invocation. command was `./eval-runner --model /artifacts/redwood-open-3b-q8 --suite mteb-like --topk 100 --seed 42 --batch-size 64`

CI summary (abridged):
```
dataset       baseline.MRR   q8.MRR   delta
msmarco       0.354          0.272    -23.2%
trec-covid    0.421          0.413     -1.9%
argoverse     0.198          0.164    -17.2%
avg           0.324          0.283    -12.7%
```
NDCG@10 shows +0.5% overall.

jon: interesting that NDCG up but MRR down — smells like top-1 ordering flips but not gross rank changes. two quick hypotheses: 1) quantization changed embedding norm scale -> cosine normalization edge cases, 2) evaluation runner uses mixed precision accumulation somewhere causing nondeterministic ordering.

mira: i dumped sample embeddings for ms marco (first 5 queries) from both fp16 baseline and q8 artifact. link: https://artifacts/internal/dumps/1869001220/samples.jsonl. quick peek: some queries have sign flips on certain dims, norms slightly different.

alex: reproduced locally with the same artifact. small script I ran: `python scripts/compare_embs.py --a baseline/fp16 --b q8 --topk 10 --save diffs.json`

sample diff output (one query):
```
query_id: 1423
baseline_top1: doc_100 (sim=0.713)
q8_top1:       doc_245 (sim=0.709)
baseline_norm: 1.0023
q8_norm:       0.9134
```

jon: norm drop ~9% is a red flag. if cosine sims are near each other, small norm differences after normalization can reorder neighbors. can you run `l2 norms` histogram across the corpus? also check whether quantizer applied a different scaling per-channel vs per-tensor.

mira: ran histogram; median norm(q8)=0.91 * median norm(fp16). looks like our quantize path applies a global scale but rounding accumulates bias. attaching small snippet: `np.histogram(norms_q8/norms_fp16, bins=50)` shows peak ~0.92.

ci-bot: Job 1869001220 finished — artifact produced by pipeline `quantize-artifact-v2`. Tests: eval-suite (flaky: MRR drop) — see annotations.

alex: thanks. another angle: runner does `normalize(x)` but sometimes calls `.half()` on tensors before `norm()` which can underflow/round. mira can you grep for `.half()` in eval-runner?

mira: found one line in `runners/embeddings.py`: `x = x.half(); x = x / (x.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)` — that's bad ordering. casting to half before computing norm will change the norm arithmetic vs computing norm in higher precision then casting. filing a small note in the run log.

jon: yep that's the culprit candidate. fix should be to compute norm in full precision: `norm = x.float().norm(...); x = (x / norm).half()` or keep normalization in fp32 and only cast after. also add unit test that checks stable topk across dtypes for a fixed seed.

alex: as a short-term CI mitigation we could change the eval comparator to use relative ordering tolerance: treat topk order change as significant only if sim difference > 1e-3 absolute or relative > 0.5%. but long term patch the runner.

mira: i'm pushing a branch that moves normalization to fp32 and adds a regression test that runs the runner on a small synthetic corpus with both fp16 and q8 and asserts identical top1 for the seed. will also add a thresholded assert for MRR.

jon: i'll open a PR to add a CI job that runs the synthetic dtype-stability test on quantized artifacts before promoting them. @mira can you link the test vectors?

mira: linked in PR description. also adding a short note in the docs about numerical stability in quantization bring-ups.

alex: great. once PR lands let's re-run the failing CI job. thanks all — this explains why NDCG could improve (global rank preserved) while MRR drops (top-1 flips from small sim deltas). :thumbsup:

mira: quick follow-up: bumped the normalization eps to `1e-7` in the test to simulate worst-case; the q8 ordering still flips when norm scaling differs by >6%. test added: `tests/test_dtype_stability.py::test_topk_stable_across_dtypes`

jon: nice. after merge i'll add a periodic job that aggregates per-dataset MRR deltas for quantized artifacts so we catch regression patterns.

ci-bot: Noted: follow-up job scheduled `quantize-eval-sanity-check`.
